scams.name: Pantai Cenang Jet-Ski 'Damage Compensation' Shakedown
scams.description: At a Pantai Cenang jet-ski stall between Meritus Pelangi and Casa del Mar, the operator quotes RM150 for 15 minutes — no written rental, no pre-ride photo. On return he 'finds' a chipped nose cone or 'broken steering' and demands RM500–RM2,000 cash; four or five 'friends' appear if you refuse. A 2025 viral incident saw a Chinese tourist filmed in physical confrontation over a RM1,000 demand (WorldOfBuzz, Nov 2025); NST anchors the government response in 'File complaint with consumer tribunal over Langkawi jet ski repair bill' (article 1082247). Rent only through hotel concierge or a MOTAC-licensed operator. Never surrender your passport as deposit. Photograph the ski from all angles before riding, operator in-frame, and refuse to pay any 'damage' in cash — say 'call the police, we report together.'
scams.avoidance: Rent ONLY through hotel concierge or a MOTAC-licensed operator with visible license — never a random beach stall NEVER surrender your passport as deposit — illegal; photocopy or cash only Photograph + video the jet-ski from all angles BEFORE ride with operator in frame If 'damage' claimed, REFUSE cash; say 'call the police, we report together' MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050; emergency 999 'tourist emergency Pantai Cenang'
scams.location: Pantai Cenang beach-front jet-ski stalls between Meritus Pelangi and Casa del Mar, Pantai Tengah beach, Tanjung Rhu parasail operators, Cenang Mall end of strip

scams.name: Langkawi International Airport (LGK) Coupon-Taxi Overcharge & Grab Cancellation
scams.description: You walk into LGK arrivals at Padang Matsirat and head for the coupon-taxi counter. The official rate to Pantai Cenang is RM30 — but the foreigner-facing quote is RM45–RM60. Outside, an unlicensed tout pitches RM100 for the 15-minute Cenang run. Or your Grab driver WhatsApps 'cancel please, I come now RM50 cash.' During LIMA airshow weeks (May, biennial odd years), NST warned in May 2025 (article 1214151) that fares spike 2–4x and Facebook 'LIMA transfer bundles' collect deposits for rides that never existed. Ask the coupon counter for the printed rate sheet (Pantai Cenang RM30, Kuah RM35, Datai RM90, Tanjung Rhu RM70). Pre-book a hotel transfer with name sign before arrival. Grab pickup is the signposted rideshare zone outside the terminal — accept 10–20 min wait, never switch to cash off-app.
scams.avoidance: IGNORE 'taxi?' approaches inside arrivals — use OFFICIAL coupon-taxi counter with printed rate list (Cenang RM30, Kuah RM35) Book Grab on airport Wi-Fi after luggage; wait 10–20 min at signposted rideshare zone If Grab driver asks you to cancel, YOU cancel and rebook — never switch to cash Pre-book hotel transfer — RM40 with name sign; avoid Facebook 'LIMA package' sellers Report overcharging to MOTAC 1300-88-5050 or JPJ 1-800-88-7723
scams.location: Langkawi International Airport (LGK) arrivals hall, coupon-taxi counter, airport Grab/rideshare signposted pickup zone, Padang Matsirat airport road, LIMA 25 airshow shuttle stops

scams.name: Duty-Free Fake Alcohol & Counterfeit Spirits in Kuah & Pantai Cenang
scams.description: At an unbranded shop on Jalan Pantai Cenang or near Langkawi Fair in Kuah, a 1-liter 'Johnnie Walker Black' is RM50 — genuine duty-free runs RM110–RM140. The bottle is refilled with industrial alcohol (methanol-contaminated in the worst cases); the seal looks intact but the cap rim shows micro-damage. Malay Mail 'Seven detained over fake RM100 notes used at Langkawi shops' (Aug 2025) sits in the same Kuah and Cenang shop zones. Buy only from licensed chains — Zon Duty Free, Coco Valley Duty Free, Teow Soon Huat — all display the Customs license at the entrance. Verify the holographic RMC excise sticker on the neck; without it, the bottle is counterfeit. Methanol symptoms (blurred vision, abdominal pain 12–24 hours after) are an immediate ER trip — Langkawi Hospital +60 4-966-3333.
scams.avoidance: Buy ONLY from licensed chains — Zon Duty Free, Coco Valley, Teow Soon Huat (Customs license at entrance) Check holographic RMC excise sticker on every bottle — missing = counterfeit Verify cap is flush to rim with no rotation-marks; prices 40% below licensed shops are fake Stick to sealed Tiger, Heineken, Carlsberg beer; avoid bootleg samsu/arak (methanol risk) Respect duty-free limits: 1L spirits, 1 carton cigarettes, 3 kg chocolate per adult
scams.location: Jalan Pantai Cenang strip unbranded shops, Kuah Jetty Point, Langkawi Fair complex, unlicensed outlets along Jalan Kelibang, small stalls near Eagle Square (Dataran Lang)
scams.tldr: Langkawi is Malaysia's signature duty-free island — alcohol, chocolate, and tobacco sell at 30–60% below peninsula prices, which is why counterfeit-spirits operators cluster here.

scams.name: Oriental Village SkyCab/SkyBridge Ticket Tout & 'Express Lane' Scam
scams.description: In the Oriental Village parking lot at Burau Bay, a tout intercepts you with 'skip the queue, Express Lane RM150.' He's reselling already-scanned QR codes or rebranding standard tickets — the official Panorama Langkawi Express Lane is RM120, sold only at the SkyCab lower-station ticket office. Standard SkyCab + SkyBridge is RM95 (RM85 child); the full combo with SkyDome + SkyRex + 3D Art is RM150–RM180 at the official booth. TripAdvisor 'Its a scam — Panorama Langkawi SkyCab' (review 882116678) documents the pattern. Buy only at the official office or in advance via panoramalangkawi.com, Klook, or GetYourGuide. Check SkyBridge status at panoramalangkawi.com/skybridge before paying — maintenance and weather closures are common, and unofficial resellers do not refund.
scams.avoidance: Buy tickets ONLY at official SkyCab ticket office OR panoramalangkawi.com / Klook / GetYourGuide — never from parking-lot touts Ignore 'Express Lane / VIP bundle' touts — real Express Lane is RM120 only at the official booth Check panoramalangkawi.com/skybridge status BEFORE buying — closes for maintenance Eagle Square (Dataran Lang) is FREE — no ticket exists; refuse 'skip line' pitches Shared Kilim Geopark eagle tour is RM35–RM45 — ignore RM300+ 'VIP' quotes
scams.location: Oriental Village parking lot and entrance arcade, Burau Bay SkyCab lower station approach, Kuah waterfront Eagle Square (Dataran Lang), Oriental Village third-party ticket desks
scams.tldr: Panorama Langkawi SkyCab (cable car) and SkyBridge at Oriental Village, Burau Bay are the island's most-visited paid attraction.

scams.name: Pantai Cenang Beach Massage, Henna & Hair-Braid Pressure Upsell
scams.description: Walking Pantai Cenang at sunset, a vendor offers 'just RM30 sample massage, 15 minutes.' The 15 minutes stretches to 45 with 'now almost done, one more part,' and the bill is RM250. A henna-tattoo vendor quotes RM20 for a wrist design that grows up your forearm to RM200 — and 'black henna' contains PPD chemical dye that causes contact dermatitis and blistering scars lasting months. Hair-braid vendors quote RM30 for 'a few braids' then braid your scalp across 90 minutes for RM350. Decline every beach-walk vendor — 'tidak, terima kasih' and keep walking. Book massages only at branded hotel or town spas (Ishan Spa, Alun-Alun main branch, hotel spas at The Andaman or Meritus Pelangi) — RM120–RM250 for a 60-minute genuine treatment. Avoid 'black henna' entirely — only natural brown-orange is safe.
scams.avoidance: Written quote for EXACT final price + duration BEFORE starting — 'RM30 for 15 min total, no additions' Book massage ONLY at branded hotel or TripAdvisor-rated spa — RM120–RM250 for genuine 60-min AVOID 'black henna' entirely — PPD chemical causes burn-scars Decline beach vendors firmly — 'tidak, terima kasih'; walk to hotel lobby if pressured Small cash denominations; report aggressive vendors to MOTAC 1300-88-5050
scams.location: Pantai Cenang beachfront 17:00–19:00 sunset hour, Pantai Tengah beach, Cenang Mall adjacent strip, beach-bar frontage opposite Meritus Pelangi / Holiday Villa / Casa del Mar
scams.tldr: Pantai Cenang's beachfront is lined with informal massage, henna-tattoo, and hair-braid vendors who operate a classic South-East-Asia 'quoted sample, charged full' upsell pattern.

scams.name: Island-Hopping Boat Bait-and-Switch & Pulau Payar Overcrowding
scams.description: A Pantai Cenang beach tout quotes RM35 per person for '4-island tour, lunch included.' The boat holds 30–45 people in a 20-person hull, stops are 10–15 minutes, and the eagle-feeding portion is 'canceled today' with no refund. On 29 September 2025, The Sun Daily reported eight tourists injured after a Langkawi island-hopping boat capsized; The Star followed up in November with 'Cops working with Interpol to track down syndicate linked to Langkawi boat tragedy.' Pulau Payar 'Huge scam' is the canonical TripAdvisor anchor (review 741130128). Book only with established 4-star+ operators — Dev's Adventure Tours, Naam Adventure, Langkawi Coral — RM60–RM90 shared 4-island (15-passenger max), RM180–RM250 Pulau Payar with gear included. Count life jackets on boarding — if fewer than passengers, refuse to board.
scams.avoidance: Book ONLY through TripAdvisor 4-star+ operators (Dev's, Naam, Langkawi Coral, Crystal Yacht) — RM60–RM90 shared 4-island, RM180–RM250 Pulau Payar with gear Written itinerary + boat name + max passenger count + life-jackets BEFORE paying Count life-jackets on boarding; REFUSE to board if fewer than passengers Buy Kuah Jetty ferry tickets at OFFICIAL counter inside terminal; ignore outside touts Weather check 24h before; cancellations get written refund same day (Tribunal enforcement)
scams.location: Pantai Cenang beach-tout stalls, Kuah Jetty ferry terminal (to Penang/Kuala Kedah/Satun), Pulau Payar platform operators, Teluk Burau jetty, Kilim Jetty eagle-feeding boats
